# dsh-longsession

A browser-side plugin for **DeepSeek Harness Desktop / Web** that keeps long chat sessions
from gett
ing slower as the transcript grows.
Repository: <https://github.com/asots/dsh-longsession>
Current release: **0.0.1** (first version).

The host half is an inert Loader row; all behaviour lives in `lib/client.js`. It puts a
“Collapse hi

story” toggle in the session header row and bounds the history already rendered by
the page.
## The measured problem

DSH never unloads history the page has already rendered: live appends plus every “load earlier”
keep
accumulating DOM rows. In a 4.4 MB / 11-turn session on a clean test host:

- opening the session: **892 ms** to ready, one batch render, **808 ms max long task**,
DOM 1,240 →

9,218 nodes, heap 36.6 → 57.6 MB;
- each “load earlier”: one **300–630 ms** main-thread task; rows 3

— so scrolling/paint is **not** the
bottleneck, and CSS containment measured neutral.
## What the plugin does

- **Collapse history** — calls the app’s own `SessionFace.resync()` through the `sessions`
client se

rvice. This unloads the history rows the page has already rendered and reopens the
ordinary opening

page (last two turns). Chat records, model context and the disk log are
**not** deleted.
- **Toggle*

* — while the page is not collapsed the button reads “Collapse history”. After a
collapse it reads “

History collapsed”; clicking it again restores the window that was loaded
before collapse. A restore

also turns auto-collapse off for that session, so it cannot undo
what you just restored. The saved

window (turn count and scroll offset) is stored per session in
`sessionStorage`; restoring asks the

controller for the missing pages again through
`loadOlder()`. The button reads “Restoring…” while th

at runs.
- **Session-header toggle** — registered in the app’s own
`conversation.session.header.acti
ons` row (next to agent team / mode). It appears once `trimMinRows` rows are loaded, but stays disab

led until older history is
loaded (the opening page has only two turns). A status dot sits before th

e label: amber = older history is loaded and can be collapsed;
green = already collapsed; gray = not

actionable yet (no older history, a turn is running, or
restoring). The dot uses high-contrast ligh

t/dark colors and follows the app theme. It is a
host-owned slot, not an overlay.
- **Settings page*

* — Settings → Long session shows the current page load (rows and approximate
turns, plus whether it

is collapsed) and edits the button threshold, auto-collapse
threshold, request caps and whether the

header toggle is shown.
- **Auto-collapse** — when the reader is at the live tail, no turn is runni

ng, older history
is loaded and the window exceeds `autoTrimRows` rows, it collapses once (15 s cool

down) and
marks the page collapsed, so it can still be restored.
- **Optional request cap** — lowers

`maxMessages` / `turnWindow.minTurns` in the history
request before it is sent (WebSocket `session/

follow` open frame and unary `/api` page RPC).
Default only caps `maxMessages` at 200; `minTurns` is

open frame and unary `/api` page RPC).
Default only caps `maxMessages` at 200; `minTurns` is opt-in.

## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Use the profile the host actually runs (for example `web`, or the profile a desktop build
uses). Rel
oad the page after installing: the client bundle is loaded per page.
Manual install into a profile:

1. install it as a profile dependency — e.g.
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:/absolute/path

/to/dsh-longsession`, or add
`"dsh-longsession": "link:..."` to the profile package.json and run `pn

pm install` there.
A bare copy under `node_modules/` is not enough: the desktop plugin manager quara

ntines
packages that are not listed as dependencies on its next install.
2. add the Loader row that

ships in `cordis.patch.yml` to that profile's `cordis.patch.yml`;
3. reload the page (a host restart
is needed only if the profile does not hot-reload patches).
## Configuration

Loader-row config does **not** reach the browser half in this build, so override through
`localStora

ge["dsh-longsession.config"]` (JSON) or
`window.__DSH_LONGSESSION__.setConfig({...})`, or use Settin

n.config"]` (JSON) or
`window.__DSH_LONGSESSION__.setConfig({...})`, or use Settings → Long session.
| key | default | meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | master switch (disabling stops auto-collapse and wire caps) |
| `trimMinRows`

| `120` | row count at which the header toggle appears |
| `autoTrimRows` | `600` | auto-collapse t

hreshold (`0` disables it) |
| `historyMaxMessages` | `200` | cap for history `maxMessages` (`0` = o

ff) |
| `historyMinTurns` | `0` | cap for `turnWindow.minTurns` (`0` = off; `1` halves the opening p

age) |
| `historyCapsAllSessions` | `false` | apply request caps to subagents/other sessions too |
|
`showDock` | `true` | show the header toggle |
## Test
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Open `http://127.0.0.1:17772/harness.html`; the page runs 43 assertions (wire clamp,
collapse/resync

, restore via `loadOlder()`, auto-collapse, header and settings slot
registration, subscriber update

s, dispose) and prints `ALL PASS`.
`window.__TEST_RESULTS__` is machine-readable.
## Known limits

- Compacting restores the last two turns. A reader deep in old history loses the current
scroll posi

tion; the button is disabled while a turn runs.
- “History collapsed” is not instant: the old pages

are re-fetched from the host through
`loadOlder()`, one page at a time. The saved scroll offset is a

pplied afterwards on a
best-effort basis; exact pixel restoration is not guaranteed.
- The toggle is

visible in long pages but disabled until older history is loaded. A freshly
opened session is alrea

dy at the last two turns, so use “load earlier” first.
- Auto-collapse only runs at the live tail; a

reader parked above the tail is never surprised.
- An explicit restore turns automatic collapse off

for the rest of that session; a new session
starts with automatic collapse on again.
- Collapsing i

s per session: only the currently open session has a rendered page history to drop.
